newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch building workers get CPI-plus wage rise.
newsitem.headline: Dutch building workers get CPI-plus wage rise.

text.p: The Dutch Building Employers Organisation (AVBB) said on Friday it had agreed a new wage agreement for the building sector's 180,000 workers under which they will receive structural increases above inflation.
It said the workers would receive structural wage rises of 75 basis points on each of April 1, 1997 and April 1, 1998 and a one-off increase of 75 basis points on October 1, 1998.
The AVBB said they would also get inflation adjustments of 2.25 percent on July 1, 1997 and 2.75 percent on July 1, 1998.
The deal was agreed by employers and unions after nine rounds of negotiations.
A AVBB spokesman said the wage rises in excess of the increase in the consumer price index (CPI) reflected the fact that the building industry was performing well.
But he told Reuters the one-off payment showed that employers were not certain that conditions would remain so buoyant.
